decisions.quote:
In two experiments, we examined the impact of social identity and intergroup dynamics

on moral hypocrisy. Although we were unable to replicate prior findings in both minimal groups

and natural groups (Valdesolo & DeSteno, 2007), we did observe evidence of intergroup biases

in moral judgements in two ways.
decisions.reason: Dependencies resolved first: (1) Record type is 'replication' because the study collects new experimental data across two US Prolific samples (Experiment 1, N = 610 minimal groups; Experiment 2, N = 606 political groups) to re-test a prior published finding. (2) The tested original identity for row 1878 (paired with blind target 0) is Valdesolo & DeSteno (2007), 'Moral hypocrisy: social groups and the flexibility of virtue' (10.1111/j.1467-9280.2007.01961.x). (3) For the original-specific outcome, the authors explicitly state an overall replication failure verdict in the Abstract ('the results did not replicate the original findings'), Statement of Relevance ('we were unable to replicate the findings from the original paper'), Results 4.1.1 (the focal replication contrast H1 was nonsignificant and statistically equivalent to zero, F(1, 536) = 0.15, p = 0.70, 'which fails to replicate the original research'), Discussion ('unable to replicate prior findings in both minimal groups and natural groups (Valdesolo & DeSteno, 2007)'), and Conclusion ('failed to replicate the results of Valdesolo & DeSteno (2007)'). Novel extension findings (moderation by collective identification in minimal groups and out-group derogation in partisan groups) are explicitly framed as extensions and do not override the governing overall replication verdict under Codebook Step 3 Rule 1. Both shipped and blind correctly code outcome as 'failed'.
